recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is +14.8% above baseline (72.9 vs 63.5 ms), indicating strong parasympathetic resilience
Resting HR is -5.6% below baseline (48.8 vs 51.6 bpm), supporting recovery
Sleep remains chronically low (4.9h avg, 15/14 days <7h), undermining neural and metabolic repair
ACWR = 0.9 — optimal range — but recovery balance = +0.27 is only marginally positive (avg 4w = 0.0), meaning load and recovery are nearly balanced, not robustly in surplus

readiness.guidance: You’re holding steady physiologically but running on chronically insufficient sleep — prioritize sleep consolidation before adding intensity or volume.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows reduced volume and pace consistency versus last month, with a notable drop in cadence and rise in aerobic TE — suggesting fatigue or reduced neuromuscular efficiency, though VO2max and HRV continue improving.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +33 spm this month (151 vs 118) — an outlier driven by unusually high values in recent runs (157–159 spm), inconsistent with prior months and likely reflecting shorter, more frequent strides in lower-volume, fresher efforts rather than true neuromuscular adaptation.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 82.4 km would require 59.8 km across 9 sessions — ~6.6 km/session — but current readiness (low training readiness score, chronic sleep debt, marginal recovery balance) makes this unsustainable and counterproductive; chasing volume now risks regression in aerobic decoupling and efficiency.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with elevated aerobic decoupling
insights.body: Despite HRV and resting HR improvements, aerobic decoupling median has risen to 7.11% (recent: 9.37%, 7.09%) — well above the 5% aerobic threshold — and aligns with 15 of last 14 nights <7h sleep; poor sleep impairs mitochondrial biogenesis and lactate clearance, increasing drift.

insights.title: ACWR masks underlying recovery fragility
insights.body: ACWR = 0.9 appears optimal, yet recovery balance (+0.27) is barely positive and training readiness (33.5 avg) is critically low — indicating autonomic readiness lags behind mechanical load tolerance, a classic sign of accumulated neural fatigue.

insights.title: Pace-HR dissociation suggests compensatory effort
insights.body: Avg pace slowed (+11 sec/km) while avg HR dropped (-4 bpm) and aerobic TE improved (-0.5), implying reduced cardiovascular strain per unit pace — but running economy worsened (+0.32 ml/kg/km) and vertical oscillation rose (7.8–7.9 cm), pointing to less economical movement at same HR.

insights.title: Z3 dominance without Z5 stimulus erodes speed reserve
insights.body: This month’s zone distribution is 41% Z3 (aerobic-anaerobic transition) but 0% Z5 — unlike last month’s 4% Z5 — and best efforts show no new 1k/400m progress since June 11; speed maintenance requires targeted neuromuscular work, not just threshold volume.

recommendations.action: Perform three 30-min Zone 2 runs (HR ≤135 bpm) on Mon/Wed/Fri, focusing on relaxed breathing and stride rhythm — no pace target, no watch feedback beyond HR.
recommendations.reason: Zone 2 sustains aerobic development without taxing recovery reserves; current HRV and resting HR support this, and it directly counters rising decoupling by reinforcing efficient fuel use.

recommendations.action: Implement strict sleep hygiene: lights out by 22:30, no screens after 21:30, and 15-min guided breathwork at bedtime — track sleep hours daily and aim for ≥6.0h on 5+ nights this week.
recommendations.reason: 15/14 nights <7h sleep is the strongest modifiable driver of impaired decoupling, reduced efficiency, and low training readiness — addressing this yields faster ROI than adding volume or intensity.

recommendations.action: Replace one scheduled run with 10 min barefoot mobility drills (ankle circles, single-leg balance, glute bridges) + 5 min diaphragmatic breathing (5-sec inhale/6-sec exhale).
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation (7.5–7.9 cm) and ground contact time (283–370 ms) show movement inefficiency; neuromuscular priming improves economy without cardiac load.

risk_flags.evidence: Training readiness 7d avg = 33.5 (scale 0–100); sleep <7h on 15 of last 14 days; recovery balance only marginally positive (+0.27) despite optimal ACWR
risk_flags.action: Pause all Z4+ efforts and race-pace work until training readiness avg ≥45 and ≥5 nights ≥6h sleep achieved

risk_flags.evidence: Latest decoupling = 9.37% (above 5% threshold); median of last 6 = 7.11%; last 3 readings: 9.37, 7.09, 11.2 — upward trend despite stable VO2max
risk_flags.action: Eliminate all runs >60 min until decoupling median falls below 5% for 3 consecutive sessions

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish efficient movement patterns and autonomic regulation before progressing load — prioritize rhythm, breath, and sleep over pace or distance.
suggested_sessions: Strides + Cadence Drill (6 × 15-sec strides @ 165 spm, walk recovery)
